newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian industry welcomes law reform plan.
newsitem.headline: Australian industry welcomes law reform plan.

text.p: The Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry (ACCI) said on Tuesday the government's corporate law economic reform programme would give great encouragement to industry.

"It responds most effectively to calls ... for the legal system in Australia to better reflect commercial realities, rapidly changing technologies and an increasingly internationally-based market place," ACCI chief executive Mark Paterson said in a statement.

Australian Treasurer Peter Costello announced earlier on Tuesday that the government was inviting public comment on the reform of corporate law in several areas, including fundraising, takeovers, and directors' duties.

Paterson said the current corporate law simplification programme, which had been under operation for the past few years, was inadequate and failed to address the basic impediments to industry competitiveness.
"The areas now targeted for reform by the Treasurer's announcement ... are all important in determining the competitiveness of Australian business," he said.
"Overall, this corporate law reform package is a major step towards a more integrated approach to economic planning and management."
